html:
On 21 August 1415 a Portuguese fleet led by King John I and his sons took Ceuta, a Muslim port on the African side of the Strait of Gibraltar. It was the first step of Portugal's overseas empire.

Ceuta was a rich trading town at the end of caravan routes across the Sahara. The Portuguese hoped for gold, glory against Islam, and a base against pirates. They took it in a single day. But the caravans moved to other ports, and holding Ceuta was costly.

The king's son Henry, who fought there, turned to sending ships down the African coast. That path led to the voyage of Vasco da Gama to India. Ceuta stayed with Spain when Portugal broke away in 1640 and is still Spanish today. See Portugal and Morocco.
sum: On 21 August 1415 a Portuguese fleet led by King John I and his sons took Ceuta, a Muslim port on the African side of the Strait of Gibraltar. It was the first step of Portugal's overseas empire.
